title: ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui
text: AG-UI: the Agent-User Interaction Protocol. Bring Agents into Frontend Applications. https://ag-ui.com The open protocol that connects any agent to any app. Docs · Examples · Spec · Discord AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications. Agents don't fit the request/response model. They stream tokens, call tools mid-response, update shared state, pause for a human, and spawn subagents, and every framework does it differently. AG-UI replaces that custom wiring with one bi-directional event stream: the agent emits typed events, and any client can render them, no matter which framework built the agent. The same agent can power a web app, a mobile app, a terminal, or Slack. Important AG-UI 1.0 is here. The protocol now has a stable, frozen specification backed by a JSON Schema, and the TypeScript, Python, and .NET SDKs are generated from it. 1.0 is backwards compatible in both directions: 0.x agents work with 1.0 clients and vice versa. What changed → · Migration guide → Quick start Start a new app. The CLI scaffolds a frontend (CopilotKit on Next.js, or a terminal client) wired to the agent framework you pick: npx create-ag-ui-app@latest Then follow the printed next steps. The generated templates call OpenAI, so set your key before npm run dev: export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..." Or speak the protocol directly: a 30-line agent server and client An AG-UI agent is any HTTP endpoint that accepts a RunAgentInput and streams events back. No API keys needed for this one. 1. The agent (Python). Requires Python 3.9+. pip install ag-ui-protocol fastapi uvicorn # server.py import uuid from fastapi import FastAPI, Request from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse from ag_ui.core import ( PROTOCOL_VERSION, RunAgentInput, RunStartedEvent, RunFinishedEvent, TextMessageStartEvent, TextMessageContentEvent, TextMessageEndEvent, ) from ag_ui.encoder import EventEncoder app = FastAPI() @app.post("/") async def run_agent(input_data: RunAgentInput, request: Request): encoder = EventEncoder(accept=request.headers.get("accept")) async def events(): yield encoder.encode(RunStartedEvent( thread_id=input_data.thread_id, run_id=input_data.run_id, protocol_version=PROTOCOL_VERSION, )) message_id = str(uuid.uuid4()) yield encoder.encode(TextMessageStartEvent(message_id=message_id, role="assistant")) for chunk in ["Hello ", "from ", "AG-UI!"]: yield encoder.encode(TextMessageContentEvent(message_id=message_id, delta=chunk)) yield encoder.encode(TextMessageEndEvent(message_id=message_id)) yield encoder.encode(RunFinishedEvent(thread_id=input_data.thread_id, run_id=input_data.run_id)) return StreamingResponse(events(), media_type=encoder.get_content_type()) uvicorn server:app --port 8000 2. The client (TypeScript). In a second terminal, in a new folder. Requires Node.js 20+. npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module npm install @ag-ui/client tsx // client.ts import { HttpAgent } from "@ag-ui/client"; const agent = new HttpAgent({ url: "http://localhost:8000/" }); agent.addMessage({ id: crypto.randomUUID(), role: "user", content: "Hi there!" }); await agent.runAgent({}, { onRunStartedEvent: ({ event }) => console.log(`run started (AG-UI ${event.protocolVersion})`), onTextMessageContentEvent: ({ event }) => { process.stdout.write(event.delta); }, onRunFinishedEvent: () => console.log("\nrun finished"), }); npx tsx client.ts You should see Hello from AG-UI! stream in. Swap the server for any supported framework and the client doesn't change. Where AG-UI fits AG-UI is one of three open, complementary agentic protocols. MCP gives agents tools and context, A2A lets agents work with other agents, and AG-UI brings agents to users. A single agent often uses all three, and AG-UI can front agents that speak MCP or A2A. Read more → Note AG-UI or A2UI? They work together. A2UI, MCP Apps, and Open-JSON-UI are generative UI specs: they describe what UI an agent wants to show. AG-UI is the runtime protocol that carries those payloads, along with everything else, between the agent and the app. Learn more → Integrations AG-UI is adopted by Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Oracle, and built into most agent frameworks. Every framework below has a live demo in the Dojo. Building block What it does Try it Streaming chat Token-by-token messages across multi-turn sessions, with cancel and resume Demo Generative UI Agents render typed components, or declarative UI with A2UI and MCP Apps Demo Shared state A typed store the agent and app both read and write, synced with snapshots and JSON Patch deltas Demo Frontend tools The agent calls tools that run in the app, and gets the result back Demo Human in the loop Runs end with an interrupt outcome; the user approves, edits, or rejects, and the next run resumes Demo Reasoning Show the agent's reasoning as it works, including encrypted reasoning round-trips Demo Subagents Nested delegation, with every event attributed to the subagent run that produced it Demo Multimodal Images, audio, video, and documents in user input and tool results Demo Tool output streaming, backend tool rendering, activity progress, token usage, and custom events are covered in the docs. Here's a quick tour of the Dojo: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c298eea8-3f39-4a94-b968-7712429b0c49 How it works Your app starts a run by sending the agent a single RunAgentInput: the conversation, the tools the frontend offers, shared state, and context. The agent answers with a stream of typed events from eight families: run lifecycle, text messages, tool calls, state, reasoning, activity, subagents, and custom events (full list). Only the run lifecycle is required, so a minimal agent emits a handful of events and grows from there. AG-UI is transport-agnostic. The spec defines HTTP + SSE and a binary HTTP + Protobuf binding, and middleware can adapt events from any source. Read the architecture overview for the full picture. Event reference AG-UI 1.0 defines 31 event types in eight families. See the spec for every field. Event family Events Runs and steps RUN_STARTED RUN_FINISHED RUN_ERROR STEP_STARTED STEP_FINISHED Text messages TEXT_MESSAGE_START TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT TEXT_MESSAGE_END TEXT_MESSAGE_CHUNK Tool calls TOOL_CALL_START TOOL_CALL_ARGS TOOL_CALL_END TOOL_CALL_RESULT TOOL_CALL_CHUNK State STATE_SNAPSHOT STATE_DELTA (JSON Patch) MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT Reasoning REASONING_START REASONING_MESSAGE_* REASONING_ENCRYPTED_VALUE REASONING_END Activity ACTIVITY_SNAPSHOT ACTIVITY_DELTA Subagents SUBAGENT_STARTED SUBAGENT_FINISHED SUBAGENT_ERROR Passthrough RAW CUSTOM Community Questions and ideas: Discord and GitHub Discussions Bugs: GitHub Issues What's next: the roadmap and the draft spec Contributing Contributions are welcome: new integrations, SDKs, docs, and fixes.
